name: Draft a Budget Justification
description: Budget narrative for a grant proposal
prompt:
Work in this order:
1. Inspect all supplied files, data, and user inputs; identify the intended audience, destination, and evidence available.
2. Resolve only ambiguities that materially change the result by asking the minimum set of blocking questions together via the interview tool.
3. Execute the task-specific requirements below exactly, preserving source meaning, values, units, citations, and uncertainty.
4. Verify factual accuracy, internal consistency, accessibility, and every claim or design choice against the supplied evidence.
5. Complete every specified artifact and chat handoff; report limitations and every saved path.

Task-specific requirements:
Draft a budget justification narrative for a grant proposal on: {topic}, with a total budget target of {budget}. Organize by standard categories: personnel (PI, co-investigators, postdocs, students, staff, with roles, percent effort, and contribution to the work), equipment, supplies/consumables, travel, publication/other direct costs, and a note on indirect costs if relevant. Justify each line item specifically in terms of the proposed research rather than with generic language, and tie effort and purchases to particular aims or tasks. Use realistic, clearly-labeled estimates; never present invented figures as institution-verified, and flag rates, salaries, or quotes that the applicant must confirm with [VERIFY]. Keep totals internally consistent with the target. If essential details (duration, key personnel, or major equipment) are missing or ambiguous, ask the minimum set of blocking questions together via the interview tool; otherwise state your assumptions. Save the budget justification as a well-named Markdown file in the sandbox for preview and download, and summarize it briefly in chat.
